context_rules.description: A general health status phrase meaning the patient is healthy. Any entity within this phrase (e.g. a spurious extraction of FIT as faecal immunochemical test) must be negated. This is a safety net; the extraction layer should not produce FIT entities from this phrase.
context_rules.example: patient fit and well → do not code 'faecal immunochemical test'

context_rules.description: Shortened form of 'fit and well'. Same semantics -- general health status, not a clinical test.
context_rules.example: fit well → no codable finding

context_rules.description: Confirms the patient is in adequate health for a procedure or activity. Not a codable disorder or test.
context_rules.example: medically fit for surgery → no codable finding for the word fit

context_rules.description: Doctors use 'nil' as a shorthand for 'none' or 'nothing'. When it appears before a condition, it means the patient does NOT have that problem. Scope is kept tight (3 tokens) because GP shorthand often lists separate findings after a period (e.g. 'nil #s. medial CPPD.') and 'nil' should only negate the immediately following term.
context_rules.example: nil chest pain → the patient has no chest pain

context_rules.description: Means the doctor looked for something and could not find it. The condition was ruled out.
context_rules.example: no evidence of infection → no infection was found

context_rules.description: Similar to 'no evidence of' — the doctor checked and found nothing to suggest the condition is present.
context_rules.example: no evidence of spread → the cancer has not spread

context_rules.description: Short for 'family history'. The condition is in a relative, not the patient. It should not be coded as the patient's own diagnosis.
context_rules.example: fhx breast cancer → a family member has breast cancer, not the patient

context_rules.description: Another shorthand for 'family history' (written with a colon). The condition belongs to a relative, not the patient.
context_rules.example: FH: diabetes → a family member has diabetes

context_rules.description: Tells the system the note is about the patient's mother. Anything near this word should be linked to the mother, not coded to the patient.
context_rules.example: mum had bowel cancer → the patient's mother had bowel cancer, not the patient

context_rules.description: Tells the system the note is about the patient's father. Conditions near this word belong to the father, not the patient.
context_rules.example: dad had a stroke → the patient's father had a stroke

context_rules.description: Short for 'history of'. The condition happened in the past and may no longer be active. It should be recorded as historical.
context_rules.example: h/o hypertension → the patient used to have high blood pressure

context_rules.description: Another way of writing 'history of'. The condition is from the patient's past, not a current problem.
context_rules.example: hx of depression → the patient had depression before

context_rules.description: The patient is waiting for something that has been arranged but not yet completed. The procedure or appointment is confirmed as planned.
context_rules.example: awaiting colonoscopy → the colonoscopy is booked but not done yet

context_rules.description: An appointment or procedure has been confirmed and arranged but has not yet taken place.
context_rules.example: booked for cystoscopy → the procedure is scheduled, not yet done

context_rules.description: The patient is on a confirmed queue for a procedure or appointment that has not happened yet.
context_rules.example: waiting list for hip replacement → the operation has not been done yet

context_rules.description: A Two-Week Wait cancer referral. The cancer is a current clinical suspicion (possible), not a confirmed diagnosis. The referral itself was placed, but the diagnosis is uncertain.
context_rules.example: 2ww referral for suspected bowel cancer → bowel cancer is suspected right now, not confirmed

context_rules.description: A referral has been made and sent. The patient has not yet been seen by the receiving service.
context_rules.example: referred for physiotherapy → physiotherapy has not started

context_rules.description: A referral has been submitted. The downstream appointment or procedure has not yet taken place.
context_rules.example: referral for gastroscopy → the procedure has not happened yet

context_rules.description: The patient is confirmed on a waiting list for something that has not yet been done.
context_rules.example: on waiting list for knee surgery → surgery has not taken place

context_rules.description: An appointment or procedure has been put in the diary. It has a confirmed date but has not happened yet.
context_rules.example: scheduled for CT scan → the scan has not been done

context_rules.description: Something is confirmed as intended to happen. It has not taken place yet.
context_rules.example: planned hysterectomy → the operation has not been performed

context_rules.description: The patient said no. The procedure or treatment was offered but refused. It should not be coded as if it happened.
context_rules.example: declined colonoscopy → the patient refused; the procedure was not done

context_rules.description: The patient explicitly refused something that was offered to them.
context_rules.example: patient declined referral to oncology → the patient said no to the referral

context_rules.description: Short for 'patient declined' — the patient said no.
context_rules.example: pt declined further investigation → no further tests were done

context_rules.description: The patient refused to do or undergo something.
context_rules.example: patient declined to undergo biopsy → the biopsy was not done

context_rules.description: The patient refused a treatment or investigation. It should not be coded as if the event took place.
context_rules.example: refused blood test → the patient said no; the test was not done

context_rules.description: The patient explicitly refused something that was offered.
context_rules.example: patient refused chemotherapy → chemotherapy was not given

context_rules.description: The patient chose not to have something. It was their decision to decline.
context_rules.example: did not want colonoscopy → the patient chose not to have the procedure

context_rules.description: Something the patient has said they do not want. The treatment or investigation was not carried out.
context_rules.example: further treatment not wanted by patient

context_rules.description: The patient does not wish to have something. They are actively choosing to decline.
context_rules.example: does not want referral at this time → no referral was made

context_rules.description: The patient has specifically said no to a course of treatment.
context_rules.example: declined treatment with statins → statins were not prescribed

context_rules.description: The patient has said no to being referred to another service.
context_rules.example: declined referral to breast clinic → the patient was not referred

context_rules.description: An appointment or treatment was cancelled before it happened. It should not be coded as completed.
context_rules.example: appointment cancelled → the patient was not seen

context_rules.description: The patient themselves rang up and cancelled. The appointment did not happen.
context_rules.example: patient cancelled colonoscopy appointment → procedure not done

context_rules.description: The appointment was cancelled by any party. The event did not take place.
context_rules.example: appointment cancelled due to patient illness

context_rules.description: The patient missed their appointment without cancelling. The consultation or procedure did not happen.
context_rules.example: did not attend clinic → no review took place

context_rules.description: Short for 'Did Not Attend' — the patient missed an appointment. This is NHS shorthand and does not mean DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid). allowed_types=[] restricts firing to standalone usage only.
context_rules.example: DNA colonoscopy → the patient did not turn up; the procedure was not done

context_rules.description: Past tense of DNA — the patient previously missed an appointment.
context_rules.example: dna'd last month → the patient missed their appointment last month

context_rules.description: A brief reference to something, often from the past. The condition may have been raised in passing rather than being a current issue.
context_rules.example: patient mentioning previous chest pain → past symptom, not a current complaint

context_rules.description: Information about the patient's past medical history. Conditions listed under 'Background:' are historical and may not be active now.
context_rules.example: Background: hypertension, T2DM → these are existing long-term conditions, not new diagnoses

context_rules.description: The clinical reason a referral or investigation is being requested. The condition listed is a current clinical suspicion, not a confirmed diagnosis and not a future event.
context_rules.example: Reasons for request: possible colorectal cancer → current suspicion, not a confirmed diagnosis

context_rules.description: Background details provided to support a referral. The conditions and symptoms mentioned are current clinical concerns, not confirmed diagnoses.
context_rules.example: Clinical information: rectal bleeding, weight loss → current symptoms prompting investigation

context_rules.description: Eligibility criteria being checked for a referral or treatment. The condition is a current clinical concern being assessed, not confirmed.
context_rules.example: criteria: meets 2ww threshold for lung cancer referral → current suspicion being evaluated

context_rules.description: Clinical probability but not certainty. The condition is suspected rather than confirmed.
context_rules.example: likely deconditioning → possible, not confirmed

context_rules.description: Partial speculative qualifier. The clinician suspects some degree of the condition.
context_rules.example: likely some central sensitisation → possible finding

context_rules.description: Clinical suspicion approaching but not reaching certainty.
context_rules.example: probably viral → possible cause

context_rules.description: Clinician believes this is the most likely explanation but has not confirmed it.
context_rules.example: probable IBS → possible diagnosis

context_rules.description: Active clinical suspicion; investigation underway or planned to confirm.
context_rules.example: suspected DVT → possible diagnosis

context_rules.description: Longhand for '?' -- the condition is a differential or under investigation.
context_rules.example: query PE → possible pulmonary embolism

context_rules.description: Explicit uncertainty about whether the condition is present.
context_rules.example: possible anxiety → uncertain

context_rules.description: Findings are compatible with this diagnosis but do not confirm it.
context_rules.example: consistent with viral URTI → possible

context_rules.description: The finding may indicate the condition but other explanations exist.
context_rules.example: may represent early fibrosis → possible

context_rules.description: Clinical impression, not a confirmed diagnosis.
context_rules.example: appears to be cellulitis → possible

context_rules.description: Tentative clinical impression.
context_rules.example: might be sciatica → possible

context_rules.description: Differential diagnosis under consideration.
context_rules.example: could be early COPD → possible

context_rules.description: Clinical impression section -- conditions listed are working hypotheses, not confirmed.
context_rules.example: Impression: tension headache → possible diagnosis
